item.title: MotoGP Malaysian GP: Alex Marquez claims pole from Marc Marquez; Jorge Martin out
item.description: Motorsport photo Alex Marquez edged out his elder brother Marc Marquez to claim pole position for the Malaysian Grand Prix, as Ducati dominated Saturday morning’s qualifying at Sepang. While reigning MotoGP champion Marc Marquez had been the fastest rider at Sepang on Friday, Gresini’s Alex Marquez went quicker when it mattered, beating him to the top spot in Q2 by just 0.070s. Pedro Acosta completed the front row for KTM, while Ai Ogura emerged as the top Aprilia rider in fourth ahead of Marco Bezzecchi. Just minutes into the start of Q1, Aprilia announced that championship contender Jorge Martin will sit out the remainder of the weekend due to injury, boosting Marc Marquez’s hopes of winning a 10th title. Marquez had already set the pace in Friday practice, but as Q2 began it was his younger brother Alex who laid the initial benchmark, posting a time of 1m56.697s in the first five minutes to take to the top. Marc Marquez also managed to break the 1m57s barrier on his first run, but ended up more than three tenths of the reigning Malaysian GP winner. Pedro Acosta emerged as Ducati’s closest rival in the first half of the session, while Marco Bezzecchi and Ai Ogura stood fifth and seventh on the two surviving Aprilia bikes. As the second runs began, the Noale-based manufacturer rose to the fore, with Bezzecchi edging out Alex Marquez by 0.029s before Ogura went even quicker on a 1m56.617s. However, Ducati still had more speed on tap, with Marc Marquez demoting Ogura to second despite suffering some wild moments on his factory GP26. Utimately, it was Alex Marquez who ended qualifying on time, the 30-year-old asserting his authority at Sepang - where he won last year - with a time of 1m56.493s. With no late changes to the order at the front, the Marquez brothers locked out the top two spots on the grid, with Acosta continuing his strong form from Friday to grab third place. Acosta’s late effort relegated Aprilia to the second row, with Ogura ending up fourth for Trackhouse ahead of factory rider Bezzecchi. Fabio di Giannantonio wound up sixth for VR46, while Tech3’s Enea Bastianini ended up seventh after topping FP3 earlier on Saturday. Honda’s charge was led by Johann Zarco in eighth, the Frenchman coming from Q1 to book a spot on the third row. Francesco Bagnaia also progressed from Q1 but smashed the windscreen of his Ducati in anger after losing half a second in the third sector. He eventually qualified ninth, behind the year-old GP25 of VR46 rider Franco Morbidelli. Joan Mir (Honda) and Maverick Vinales (Tech3) completed the top 12. Factory Honda rider Luca Marini missed out on a Q2 slot by seven hundredths of a second, ending up 13th on the grid ahead of the LCR-entered RC213V of Honda rookie Diogo Moreira. Brad Binder couldn’t join the rest of the KTM contingent in the second part of qualifying, finishing almost eight tenths off the pace in 15th. item.title: St. Cloud State's Jack Reimann exits game in loss vs. Arizona State
item.description: ST. CLOUD — St. Cloud State men’s hockey senior center and captain Jack Reimann exited the game in the first period holding his shoulder and did not return in the Huskies’ 3-2 loss against Arizona State in the NCHC opener on Oct. 30. He is still being evaluated for injury. Reimann has played in all five games this season and this was his 101st career game with the Huskies, accumulating four goals and 11 assists in his four seasons. “You can never have enough of that [leadership],” head coach Nick Oliver said. “I thought our guys handled it well, especially in a game like tonight. You miss that veteran presence and what Jack brings, so we’re hoping we get good news on that.” Jack's father, Dan Reimann , played for the Huskies from 1992-96 and spent four seasons in the ECHL with the Johnstown Chiefs, Louisville Riverfrogs and Florida Everblades. Prior to the Huskies, Jack played three seasons of junior hockey in the NAHL with the St. Cloud Norseman (2020-21) and the USHL with the Sioux Falls Stampede (2021-22), the Muskegon Lumberjacks (2022-23) and the Des Moines Buccaneers (2022-23). A Ham Lake, Minn. native, Jack is a 2021 Blaine High School graduate where he played three seasons, scoring 20 goals and racking up 40 assists in 73 games, leading the Bengals to a third-place finish at the 2019 Minnesota Class AA State Tournament. In Reimann's absence, the Huskies entered the second period tied 2-2 with goals from junior Gavyn Thoreson and sophomore Noah Urness in the first. After a scoreless second period, the Huskies surrendered the game-winner to Arizona State's Jack Beck in the third period. "When you take a center out of your lineup and down to 11 forwards for 50 minutes of that game, it puts some more miles on other guys' tires," Oliver said. "We're going to be in that same game over and over in our league. I think we can learn through a night like tonight, good and bad. I don't think we worked hard enough to get to the inside of the rink, and as the game went, our ability to earn second and third opportunities around their goalie were more limited than in the first." The Huskies are back in action on Oct. 31 against Arizona State to try and even the series. item.title: Why Godby wanted to make a statement in 50-10 win over Lincoln
item.description: In a town with no formal city championship, Amos P. Godby wanted to ensure that there was no doubt about who the best high school football team in Tallahassee was. “It’s been a lot of talk about city champs and who runs the city; who’s the best in the city? We wanted to make sure that it wasn’t a question after the game,” Godby head coach John Holston told the Tallahassee Democrat after the game. Therefore, the Cougars made a point of securing a dominant win to cap off the regular season, beating Lincoln 50-10 at Gene Cox Stadium in Friday’s Week 11 clash. “It’s a little rivalry they want to create, but we just got to keep putting in the work to shut that down,” said Kyle Estimond , a junior wide receiver and safety for the Cougars. “We know that we’re the better team when we do what we got to do. So we came out here and executed. It was definitely one we had checked off on the schedule since the beginning of the season. Everyone was looking forward to this game: the city, all of us, the players. This week, we’ve just been really focused, trying to do what we got to do to come out with a win like this.” The Godby Cougars dominated the trenches and even nabbed three interceptions at the expense of Lincoln Trojans quarterback Thomas Hutchinson. Defensive back trio Terrian Akins Jr., Auceon Mitchell Jr., and Xavier Randolph all got a pick apiece. Three-star running back and South Alabama commit Kamren McMillan also got in on the action with a score. But the star of the show was, in fact, Estimond. The 6-foot-2 deepball threat and transfer from North Florida Christian scored four total touchdowns, three on passes from three-star quarterback Landon Dougherty . “I’m so happy he had a game like this because he deserved it,” Holston said about Estimond. “For him to go out and have this type of night, he deserves it.” Estimond’s most impressive touchdown was an 86-yard punt return, which initially looked like the Cougars were going to let the Trojans down, but he picked it up and took it to the house. Since it fell to Wakulla in a 35-34 loss , the Cougars are prepared to enter the FHSAA Class 3A playoffs as a No. 2 seed. Friday’s victory kept those hopes alive. A loss could have negatively impacted their tournament seeding, Holston shared. Since falling to Wakulla, Godby has posted two consecutive 50-point games to add to their season total of three. Last week, Oct. 23, the Cougars beat Suwannee 52-0, and earlier in the season, the Cougars traveled to Niceville and left with a 57-22 win on Oct. 2. “We dropped the ball against Wakulla, and we wanted to do after that was set the tone,” Holston said. “Let anybody know in the playoffs that if they see us, they’re going to see a lot of 50-point games back-to-back.” Teams are off next week, and then the FHSAA playoffs are set to start on Friday, Nov. 13. The No. 17 Florida Gators could be without one of their leading offensive weapons again when they face the No. 3 Georgia Bulldogs on Saturday as sophomore wide receiver Vernell Brown III was downgraded to questionable on Friday’s SEC availability report. Brown had been listed as probable on Wednesday and Thursday, raising hopes that he would return after missing Florida’s last three games with a knee injury. The Gators have been without Brown since he suffered the injury during the first half of their September 26 win over Ole Miss. His absence has coincided with a decline in Florida’s offensive production. During the team’s 4-0 opening stretch, Brown recorded 17 receptions for 271 yards and four touchdowns, including two scores on punt returns. The Gators scored 96 points across their SEC victories over Auburn and the Rebels but has managed just 63 points while going 1-2 in the three games without him. Meanwhile, things appear to be trending in a positive direction for the Gators at quarterback. Aaron Philo and Tramell Jones Jr. were both upgraded from questionable to probable on Friday. Philo is expected to start after missing last week’s 27-24 win over Texas because of a right shoulder injury. Jones filled in during that upset, helping Florida overcome the Longhorns despite taking considerable amount of contact. item.title: Chelsea vs Manchester United: Live stream, Time & How to watch
item.description: Stamford Bridge is the venue for this weekend’s pulsating Premier League lunchtime kickoff, which pits under-performing Chelsea against crisis club Manchester United. Both Xabi Alonso and Michael Carrick are at risk of losing three successive games in all tournaments this weekend, but few expected the latter to even make the trip to the capital this weekend. Still backed by a large portion of the Old Trafford faithful – which is more than can be said for the players, INEOS and the Glazer family – Carrick has earned an unforeseen stay of execution as Man United manager amid the Red Devils’ declining form. Matheus made the difference in our previous visit to Chelsea! 🇧🇷⚽️ pic.twitter.com/3wNKm7Cg9X — Manchester United (@ManUtd) October 30, 2026 In the eyes of many, Carrick was bidding farewell to the Theatre of Dreams after last weekend’s horror show against Bournemouth, who astonishingly won 3-0 away at Man United for the third time in four seasons to plunge the club into further catastrophe. Despite now overseeing an eight-game winless run in all tournaments and six-match winless sequence in the top flight – leaving Man Utd 16th in the Premier League table and just one point above the drop zone – Carrick will be given time to turn the Red Devils’ fortunes around. The expulsion of Bruno Fernandes from the XI to face Bournemouth naturally dominated the Man Utd headlines last weekend; Carrick stressed that his captain was dropped for “pure football” reasons after he appeared to criticise his manager’s tactics in Como. The pair have reportedly now held clear-the-air talks, and Fernandes should return to the Man Utd side on Saturday, after Carrick revealed in his press conference that the Portuguese remains “fully committed” to the club. Kobbie Mainoo is also back in training, but Marcus Rashford’s availability remains unclear, while Luke Shaw (unspecified), Benjamin Sesko (shin), Manuel Ugarte (knee) and Patrick Dorgu (thigh) are still missing. item.title: Who Won The NASCAR Truck Series Race at Martinsville? Full Race Results
item.description: NASCAR Craftsman Truck Series results from Martinsville. Getty Chandler Smith won a crash-filled NASCAR Craftsman Truck Series Black’s Tire 200 at the Martinsville Speedway. Smith passed his Front Row Motorsports teammate, Layne Riggs, on a restart with just 12 laps remaining. The win was Smith’s 10th career Truck Series win and third win of the season. Riggs dominated the majority of the race, sweeping both stages and totaling 20 stage points. The driver of the No. 34 led a race-high 156 of 200 laps. Ultimately, Riggs finished third. In regards to the championship battle, the fall from first to third was a major missed opportunity for Riggs in his championship hopes. As championship leader Kaden Honeycutt finished 14th, Riggs left huge points on the board after not winning. Heading into Homestead-Miami Speedway next week, the season finale race, Honeycutt leads Riggs by 20 points in the championship battle. The race was a wreckfest as it saw nine caution periods for 67 laps, including two red flags. In a race where there was no room for error, the two championship contenders survived. Tristan McKee impressed after making NASCAR history earlier in the day. The 16-year-old became the youngest pole sitter in Craftsman Truck Series history on Friday afternoon in the single-truck qualifying session. In the race, McKee was a contender throughout the evening and wound up finishing fifth, the highest among the non-Chase drivers. This stretch will prove if the Islanders’ recent success is real or just a lucky streak. Islanders defenseman Matthew Schaefer scored the overtime winner 33 seconds into the extra period to secure the 4-3 victory in St. Paul, Minnesota. His goal capped a strong road trip that saw the team get points in seven of their last eight games. The win came despite a growing injury list, including key defenseman Ryan Pulock, who left early with an upper-body injury and is expected to miss Saturday’s game. item.description: BELLEVUE — It has been an emotional week for the Cornell High School football team after losing its head coach, Ed Dawson, who died during the team’s Week 9 game against Rochester . Just hours before the team suited up and traveled to take on Northgate in Week 10 on Friday, Oct. 30, the Cornell squad attended the services for Dawson. While Cornell fell to Northgate 7-0, it was an effort Dawson would be proud of , with the team taking the game down to the wire and having a chance to tie and take the lead with seconds remaining. “He would have been so proud of this team tonight,” Cornell assistant coach and Dawson’s nephew Ken Rainey said. “We played so well for 48 minutes, with our defense strong throughout and while our offense started out slow, we made our adjustments and had a shot at the end. "We played hard and that’s all we asked out of these guys tonight.” For the past week, the entire Western Pennsylvania high school football community has wrapped their arms around the Coraopolis and Cornell communities, with touching tributes sweeping across the WPIAL, with coaching staff wearing blue wristbands and custom t-shirts. Many teams across the area, including Cornell’s opponent, Northgate, donated its 50/50 drawing to the Dawson family. With everything that transpired over the past seven days, it wouldn’t be questioned if Cornell would not want to play the game. Senior wide reciever Jaiden Swann and quarterback Ta'rell Jones got the offense humming with a pair of deep passes down the sidelines early in the first quarter, while Jeremiah Dent reignited the offensive attack late in the third quarter with a plethora of strong runs. Each time the Cornell team seemed out of the game, it made a stop or a third-down conversion to keep the team in the game until the waning moments. “This is a resilient group. item.title: Giannis Leads Heat to Dominant NBA Cup Victory
item.description: Photo by: Isabella Frias The Miami Heat opened their NBA Cup campaign in impressive fashion Friday night, taking down the Indiana Pacers 145-125 behind a monster performance from Giannis Antetokounmpo. Antetokounmpo finished with 31 points, 17 rebounds and 10 assists, recording a triple-double while controlling the game on both ends of the floor. His performance gave Miami exactly what it needed to begin its NBA Cup run with a statement victory. Miami’s Offense Takes Over The Heat had to overcome an early challenge from Indiana, which came out firing and scored 42 points in the first quarter. The Pacers carried a 42-36 advantage into the second period and appeared ready to make things difficult for Miami. However, the Heat completely changed the momentum before halftime. Miami closed the second quarter on a 22-7 run, turning a deficit into a 68-61 lead at the break. The momentum continued after halftime. Miami opened the third quarter with a 10-0 run, creating separation and putting Indiana in a difficult position. Klay Thompson played a major role in the offensive explosion, finishing with 25 points and seven three-pointers. It was one of his best performances since joining Miami and gave the Heat another dangerous scoring option alongside Antetokounmpo. Bam Adebayo also delivered a strong performance, adding 27 points and nine rebounds. Pelle Larsson contributed 18 points, while Davion Mitchell finished with 15 points and 11 assists. A Strong Start to NBA Cup Play Indiana struggled to keep pace after its impressive opening quarter. Quenton Jackson led the Pacers with 24 points, while Andrew Nembhard added 22 points and nine assists. The Heat continued scoring in the fourth quarter, putting up 42 points in the final period to secure the 20-point victory. Miami’s performance showed how dangerous this team can be when its stars are clicking together. Antetokounmpo’s ability to score, rebound and create opportunities for teammates gives the Heat a major advantage. The NBA Cup group stage is only beginning, but Miami has already made a statement. If Giannis continues playing at this level and Thompson keeps knocking down shots, the Heat could become a serious threat as the tournament moves forward.

The Arizona Diamondbacks are turning to a division rival to strengthen their pitching staff, reportedly bringing in San Diego Padres bullpen coach Ben Fritz as t heir next pitching coach . Fritz will replace Brian Kaplan, who was not retained after two seasons. Arizona has agreed to hire the 45-year-old, although final details still need to be completed before the move becomes official. Fritz has spent the past seven seasons working with San Diego’s major-league staff, taking over as bullpen coach in 2020. He also briefly served as the Padres’ interim pitching coach in 2021 after Larry Rothschild was dismissed. This will be his first full-time opportunity in the position. Before entering coaching, Fritz was a standout at Fresno State and a first-round selection by the Oakland Athletics in the 2002 MLB Draft. He spent seven seasons pitching in the minor leagues before joining the Padres organization as a coach in 2015. Fritz is expected to work with returning assistant pitching coach Owen Dew and bullpen coach Wellington Cepeda. Arizona is reportedly keeping the rest of its coaching staff intact , making Kaplan’s departure the only change. The Diamondbacks will need Fritz to carry some of San Diego’s success into Arizona. Improving consistency and getting more production from the pitching staff will be key priorities as the team prepares for the 2027 season. item.title: No. 8 Staples football beats Wilton behind swarming defense, 2 interceptions from Dylan Lust
item.description: Staples celebrates a touchdown against Wilton at Wilton High School on Oct. 30, 2026. (Scott Ericson/Hearst Connecticut Media) WILTON – The Staples football team did what Top 10 teams want to do on the road, putting together a dominant defensive performance Friday night to beat Wilton 24-7 and stay near the top of the Class LL playoff standings. The Staples defense smothered Wilton all night with multiple sacks and two interceptions apiece by Dylan Lust and Nate Maurillo. Three of those interceptions set the Wreckers up in good field position, leading to the first two scores of the game and then a field goal in the second half. Lust made up for two previous drops on near interceptions earlier in the season with his two picks. "The defense has really stepped up this year and it is 11 guys to the ball every single play," Lust said. "I have had two dropped picks this season, but coach believed in me and put me in a good opportunity to make plays." Nick Triscari scored the first on an 11-yard run in the first quarter and Grant Bozeman got in on a 2-yard dive in the second to put the Wreckers up 14-0 at the break. A 38-yard field goal by David How followed Lust's second interception. Staples capped their scoring with a 7-yard touchdown run by Bozeman in the fourth quarter. Wilton coach EJ DiNunzio said his team had too many turnovers and penalties to beat Staples, the No. 8 team in the GametimeCT Top 10 Football Poll. "It was terrible," DiNunzio said. "I have to be honest, we are not talking about sophomores, it was some of our senior guys making silly mistakes. You can't turn the ball over and have bad penalties against a good team." Wilton is 3-4 and outside of the top eight in the rankings who qualify for the Class MM playoff field. Things do not get any easier for the Warriors who travel to face No. 3 ranked Greenwich next Friday at 7 p.m., before hosting No. 1 New Canaan the following week. Staples is 6-1 and is No. 3 in the Class LL playoff rankings. "Our defense does a great job week in and week out," Staples coach Matty Jacowleff said. "We preach playing with a get there mentality and swarming to the ball." Staples will travel to Norwalk next Saturday for a 2:30 game against the Bears in a game that will be played at McMahon High School. item.description: Mammoth Lightning Nikita Kucherov Getty In an original trade pitch idea, the Utah Mammoth would acquire Tampa Bay Lightning superstar Nikita Kucherov in a blockbuster trade. The internet broke on Friday night when NHL insider Elliotte Friedman reported that Kucherov, the reigning Hart Memorial Trophy winner as the NHL MVP, will not re-sign with Tampa Bay and wants a trade. Immediately, the wheels began turning on trade ideas for the Lightning’s star winger, and one team that is being linked to acquire him is the Mammoth, a team on the rise that may have the assets to get a deal done. So, could the Lightning and Mammoth link up on a trade for Kucherov? Let’s give it a shot. Mammoth, Lightning Nikita Kucherov Trade Pitch Here is this author’s original trade pitch sending Kucherov to the Mammoth. Lightning Trade: Nikita Kucherov ($9.5 million expiring contract) Mammoth Trade: Vincent Trocheck ($5.625 million for this year plus two more years) Lawson Crouse ($4.3 million expiring contract) 2027 Mammoth 1st-round draft pick (top-10 protected) 2027 Toronto Maple Leafs 3rd-round draft pick (previously acquired) 2027 Lightning 5th-round draft pick (previously acquired) From a salary cap perspective, this trade matches up almost perfectly as far as the money goes, so there is no issue there, as it’s a near match. Kucherov’s contract is up after this season, and while an extension could be part of this trade, he would likely want to see how his time in Utah goes before committing long-term to their program, so his signing an extension right away is not a mandatory part of this deal. Why Both Teams Would Do This Trade For the Mammoth, it’s clear why they would want to get Kucherov: Because he’s a proven Stanley Cup winner, and Utah is trying to become a contender. This is a young team on the rise with tons of talent up and down its lineup. Adding a true gamebreaker like Kucherov to its talented pool of young players would be absolutely incredible and would help turn the Mammoth from just a playoff team into a legitimate Stanley Cup contender this season and beyond if he re-signs with them. Mammoth owner Ryan Smith has deep pockets and would likely have no problem giving Kucherov the long-term, big-money deal that he wants and deserves, too, so if Kucherov likes it in Utah, they can re-sign him to a long-term contract extension. As for the Lightning, they would get back a solid veteran center in Trocheck who is signed for this season plus two more at a good price, plus a very underrated forward in Crouse, who could either be a rental for the rest of this season as the Lightning make a playoff run of their own, or perhaps he could be re-signed to a long-term deal if he proves to be a good fit in Tampa Bay. Plus, Tampa would pick up three draft picks as part of this trade to make it fair. So, what do you think, Mammoth and Lightning fans? Is this a fair trade for both teams? Let us know. item.title: Verstappen and Lawson given grid penalties for Mexico practice collision
item.description: Max Verstappen has won two races so far in 2026 [Reuters] Max Verstappen and Liam Lawson were both given one-place grid penalties for an incident in which they collided in Friday practice at the Mexico City Grand Prix. Verstappen accused Lawson of "not very smart behaviour" and trying to "drive me off the track at the hairpin" as the two disputed the same piece of track during the session. The four-time champion and the New Zealander clashed in the stadium section towards the end of the lap, with the two cars hitting each other side-on after running through three corners side by side. Race stewards decided that both had been at fault for the incident and took the unusual step of issuing a sporting penalty for an infringement in practice. The FIA stewards report said that Verstappen was preparing for a flying lap and Lawson on a "cool-down" lap after a timed lap "preparing for another push lap". It added: "The drivers of both cars behaved in a manner that was considered unacceptable by the stewards." It said: "Both drivers admitted the moves were unnecessary and 'clumsy'." Verstappen, speaking before the stewards' verdict, said: "Maybe not very smart behaviour what he was trying to do there. "At the end of the day it is not going to change my weekend, but if I were him I would act a little smarter and when you're fighting for your seat it's not very smart behaviour." Lawson is one of three drivers competing for two seats at Racing Bulls, Red Bull's junior team, next year, alongside current team-mate Arvid Lindblad and Bulgarian Formula 2 front-runner Nikola Tsolov, who drove for Racing Bulls in first practice on Friday. Verstappen has an influential position within the Red Bull organisation as their star driver. The Dutchman added: "When he saw me coming, he suddenly started to accelerate. I don't know what was going through his head, that he wanted to drive me off the track in the hairpin. "That's not very sensible behaviour from someone in his position, to pick a fight with me." Lawson was Verstappen's team-mate for two races at the start of 2025 before being dropped back down to the Racing Bulls junior team after disappointing performances. He had a second spell alongside Verstappen for three races this year as a substitute for regular driver Isack Hadjar after the Frenchman broke his wrist. Lawson acquitted himself more effectively on his second time in the senior team. Racing Bulls team principal Alan Permane said: "One word - unnecessary. And I say that of both of them. I haven't heard what Max has said. I'm sure he's got his opinions and I'm sure Liam has his opinion. But mine is, it's just not needed and they can both do better." item.title: LeBron James Leads 76ers Past Knicks in Thrilling NBA Cup Victory
item.description: Photo by: Bill Streicher LeBron James delivered one of his best performances of the young season Friday night, helping the Philadelphia 76ers defeat the New York Knicks 98-93 in an NBA Cup matchup. James came through when Philadelphia needed him most, making several clutch plays down the stretch to help the Sixers secure another win over the defending NBA champions. James finished with 20 points, nine rebounds and eight assists while shooting 8-of-15 from the field. His biggest contribution came in the final minutes, when the Knicks threatened to steal the game. LeBron Delivers in the Clutch Philadelphia appeared to have control for much of the night, but New York refused to go away. Jalen Brunson knocked down a three pointer with 1:32 remaining to give the Knicks a 90-89 lead and put pressure on the Sixers. James responded with a clutch fadeaway jumper over OG Anunoby with just over a minute remaining, putting Philadelphia back in front. He later added a crucial tip-in to help put the game away. It was the kind of performance Philadelphia hoped to get when it brought the veteran superstar into the organization. Even at 41 years old, James continues to show he can take over important moments and make a difference on both ends of the floor. Maxey Provides More Offensive Firepower While James led the way late, Tyrese Maxey was Philadelphia’s leading scorer with 27 points. Anfernee Simons also made a major impact, adding 21 points off the bench. For New York, Brunson finished with 24 points and six assists, while Karl-Anthony Towns recorded 22 points and 12 rebounds. The victory improved Philadelphia to 5-1 on the season and gave the Sixers their second win over the Knicks this year. With James continuing to make an impact alongside Maxey and the rest of Philadelphia’s roster, the 76ers are quickly becoming one of the teams to watch in the Eastern Conference.

item.description: Payton Pritchard Gives Celtics A Scoring Spark The Bulls Can’t Stop originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Payton Pritchard has made the Chicago Bulls’ last two visits to Boston especially difficult. The Celtics guard scored a season-high 30 points off the bench Friday, leading Boston to a 125-111 win in its NBA Cup opener. It was the second time in five days Pritchard had taken over against Chicago. He scored 28 points in just 22 minutes during Boston’s 134-99 victory Monday. item.title: Pure perfection: Fort Collins football rolls Rocky for 10-0 season
item.description: The game wasn't perfect the whole time, but the record sure is for Fort Collins High School football. The Lambkins finished off the city's first unbeaten regular season in 12 years, rolling past city rival Rocky Mountain 52-17 on Oct. 30 at French Field. Fort Collins is now 10-0 heading into the Class 5A playoffs, almost certainly with a coveted top-eight seed and a first-round bye. It was a fitting way to end this regular season for a team that has found every which way to win all fall. The Lambkins' potent passing attack was slightly off early. No problem, as the Fort Collins run game picked up the slack and then some. Diego Romero gashed the Lobos' defense on the ground with two first-half scores, and Jackson Blanchard added another, high-stepping into the endzone in style. Even though Rocky hounded quarterback Jace Garcia in the first half, the junior made enough happen on some scrambles to keep the chains moving. Then, the floodgates opened in the final two quarters. Garcia found Preston Mozer for a trio of lengthy touchdown passes (three on the night) and hit Rigoberto Galvez for another to put it away in the fourth quarter. Garcia went over 3,000 passing yards in a breakout season and is undoubtedly one of Colorado's premier QBs. The first-year starter lived up to some promising hype, accounting for 39 total touchdowns and leading a Lambkins offense that averaged over 42 points per game. Mozer finished the regular season with 13 touchdowns and threatened the 1,000-yard mark after a big season finale. Rocky (2-8, 1-5) made the Lambkins work for the perfect season in this one, coming out with an aggressive energy. The Lobos converted a fake punt, received some helpful 15-yard penalties from an overzealous Lambkins squad and got two touchdowns (one rushing, one receiving) from running back Addison Armanda. It wasn't nearly enough against one of the best city teams of the 21st century. Fort Collins still led this one 28-7 in the second quarter and then pulled away after holding a 14-point halftime advantage. The Lambkins are the first city team to finish undefeated in the regular season since Fort Collins in 2014. That team was in Class 4A. The last 5A team to go 10-0? That would be Rocky Mountain in 2008, the same year some of these seniors would have been born . This special season is nowhere near over for Fort Collins. The Lambkins should have a bye next week and then will host a 5A second-round game on Nov. 12 or 13. Fort Collins went a perfect 6-0 to take the conference title, won seven games away from home and went 4-0 in games decided by single digits. This story will be updated. Return to coloradoan.com/sports for more. Chris Abshire covers high school and community sports for the Coloradoan.
